stimulus.text: Spanish colonizers developed an elaborate caste system in the New World. At the top stood peninsulares, Spaniards born in Spain, and criollos, Spaniards born in the Americas, who together made up only one or two percent of the population. Below them came mestizos, children of Spanish men and Indigenous women, then mulattos, children of Spanish men and African women, with American Indians and Africans at the bottom. The system recognized even finer gradations, based on the specific percentage of each lineage a person possessed.

parts.prompt: Identify one group that stood at the top of the casta hierarchy.
Explain why the casta system developed so many categories.
Explain one way the casta hierarchy affected a person's life in Spanish America.

instruction: Answer each part in your own words from the stimulus only. Do not open the question file.
